An intruder rushed the stair with a cutting tool, and the fighter kept them from the junction until the analyst recorded the transmission. Between street names, a voice was counting doorways in an almost familiar neighborhood.

At street level, the analysts followed the broadcast’s first address to an empty lot. An elderly neighbor pointed to a faded line of paint on the pavement, the boundary of a house demolished before the new map was printed. She remembered who had lived behind its last doorway.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts preserved the broadcast and kept the antenna connected for a search.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s municipal crew disconnected the antenna and secured the roof.
endings.draw: The signal was recorded before shutdown, and both parties followed its first address together.

paragraphs: On a quiet coast, an abandoned weather machine opened its storm shutters every morning despite having no power. {{heroPlayer}}’s survey party came to map its mechanism; {{otherPlayer}}’s fishing families wanted the tower left alone before the night tide. A line of wet footprints ended at a sealed maintenance door.

{{hero}} found a manual crank behind the shutters and set it against the seized gears. The specialist opened the maintenance door just enough for the survey party to enter. Inside, the footprints led to a dry chair facing an old display that showed a single sentence awaiting transmission.

A fisher read the sentence aloud. It was a warning to return before the tide covered a hidden footpath, written in the hand of a relative long missing at sea. As the shutter swung shut, sunlight fell on that path for a moment, revealing the stones beneath the water.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors kept the tower open and marked the newly visible path.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s families secured the tower until the tide had passed.
endings.draw: The warning reached shore, and both parties placed markers above the submerged stones.

paragraphs: A disused quarry contained a stone amphitheater cut by workers who had vanished before its opening. {{heroPlayer}}’s explorers followed fresh tool marks into the pit; {{otherPlayer}}’s construction crew arrived to test the unstable rim. Each stone seat held a shallow bowl of collected rainwater.

{{hero}} reached the central winch as someone tried to lower a heavy block over the entrance. The fighter forced the lever back and held the mechanism long enough for the explorers to leave the pit. On the underside of the block were tiny carved seats, a model of the theater hidden in plain sight.

The construction crew braced the rim and lifted the block onto level ground. Rain began while the explorers studied the miniature, filling its carved bowls just as it filled those below. In the water, a second set of markings appeared along the little stage.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s explorers secured the amphitheater and preserved the carved model.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s construction crew closed the unstable pit and retained the site.
endings.draw: The pit remained closed while both groups copied the markings that appeared in the rain.

paragraphs: Under a crowded transit station, a forgotten platform had begun growing luminous moss over its timetable. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers brought sealed jars to collect samples; {{otherPlayer}}’s transit workers worried that the glow was drawing passengers beyond the barriers. The moss brightened whenever an approaching train sounded above.

{{hero}} watched the stair while a researcher scraped a sample from the far end of the platform. Someone tried to drag the barrier shut with the researcher behind it, and the fighter held the passage clear until the jars were carried out. Then the timetable lit up one destination at a time.

At the station entrance, a retired conductor saw the illuminated names and stopped walking. They belonged to stops removed when the lower line closed. He could still name the order in which the trains had visited them, even after the paper schedules were thrown away.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers collected the moss and kept the lower platform under observation.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s transit workers sealed the passage and held the station.
endings.draw: The platform was closed to passengers, and both groups recorded the glowing timetable.

paragraphs: A ring of old reflectors on a crater rim once sent winter sunlight to a settlement below. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to restore the mirrors; {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors reported that one reflector was aimed at an empty ledge. The settlement’s school had been without daylight for a week.

{{hero}} climbed to the misaligned reflector and released its corroded catch. The specialist turned the mirror toward the school, then saw a second beam strike the empty ledge from behind. In that brief patch of light stood a painted height chart, its highest mark beside a child’s initials.

Light spilled through the school windows as children gathered at their desks. A teacher climbed the crater path to inspect the chart. It had stood on the ledge before the school was built, and the initials belonged to the person who later designed its roof.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians held the reflector ring and restored light to the school.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors retained the rim and set the mirrors for further inspection.
endings.draw: The school received daylight, and both teams documented the unexpected beam on the ledge.

paragraphs: A butterfly conservatory had sealed itself after a humidity alarm, leaving its curator inside. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew approached through a service tunnel; {{otherPlayer}}’s horticultural team guarded fragile breeding chambers along the main aisle. Through the fogged glass, the curator could be seen carrying an empty specimen tray.

{{hero}} reached the pressure door when a stranger tried to lock it from the outer panel. The fighter pulled the panel clear and held the heavy door against its spring while the curator crawled out. She had filled the tray with paper tags, each bearing the date a butterfly had emerged.

The conservatory’s alarm stopped after the vents reopened. The curator spread her tags on a bench and pointed to an emergence date several months away. Inside the glass, the matching chrysalis was already opening, far ahead of the calendar she had kept for years.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew rescued the curator and secured the conservatory for observation.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s horticultural team retained the chambers and directed the recovery.
endings.draw: The curator emerged safely, and both teams stayed to watch the early chrysalis.

paragraphs: A vertical orchard above the city stopped releasing its pollinating drones, leaving blossoms to fall unvisited. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to repair the control room; {{otherPlayer}}’s growers wanted the drones grounded after one returned carrying a torn silk ribbon. The ribbon matched no equipment in the orchard.

{{hero}} climbed to the control room and found a cracked timing wheel beside the dormant launch rack. The specialist replaced its pin, then traced the ribbon to an upper branch where a maintenance worker had tied it around a damaged limb. Drones rose past the window as the first blossoms opened.

The worker returned to find the limb supported and the ribbon fluttering between branches. Below, children gathered petals that drifted onto the street. One drone came back with yellow pollen on its legs and settled beside the repaired timing wheel.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians retained the control room and restored the orchard’s pollination schedule.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s growers took charge of the orchard and grounded the drones for inspection.
endings.draw: The blossoms were visited, and both teams watched the repaired drones through their first cycle.

paragraphs: A river ferry terminal stood empty while its floodgates trembled under an early thaw. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers came to redirect the current; {{otherPlayer}}’s market vendors feared the detour would drown their stalls. A painted line on the terminal wall showed a flood level higher than either crew expected.

{{hero}} crawled into the gatehouse and found a secondary sluice hidden beneath stacked benches. The specialist freed its handle and turned it slowly until the river pulled away from the market steps. A faded note on the handle named the person who had added the sluice after the last great flood.

The ferry returned to the near bank as the market reopened. One vendor brought the note to an older relative, who remembered helping paint the line as a child. That night the river rose to within a handspan of it, then began to fall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers secured the gatehouse and kept the market above the diverted current.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s vendors retained the terminal and demanded another plan for the thaw.
endings.draw: Both groups kept watch at the gatehouse until the river fell below the market steps.

paragraphs: On a monastery roof, festival kites served as wind markers for a village airstrip. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came to secure the launch platform; {{otherPlayer}}’s residents had heard an aircraft circling blind in low cloud. The largest kite pulled free and caught on the stair tower.

{{hero}} reached the tower as a stranger tried to barricade its gate. The fighter shoved through, caught the kite line by hand, and kept the gate open while a resident brought down a lamp. Held taut above the roof, the kite pointed toward a break in the cloud.

The aircraft passed overhead once, then returned with its landing lights aimed at the improvised signal. After it touched down, the pilot said the last clear landmark had been the kite’s bright tail. The residents began restringing the smaller kites before the fog returned.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts held the roof platform and guided the aircraft in.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s residents kept the monastery roof and managed the airstrip signal.
endings.draw: The aircraft landed safely, and both groups helped restring the roof markers.

paragraphs: A border clinic stored temperature-sensitive medicine while a bicycle courier waited for a route through the mountains. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors came to certify its cooler; {{otherPlayer}}’s local medics feared the coming blackout would spoil the supply. The only backup battery had been fitted to an empty cabinet.

{{hero}} opened the cabinet and found the cooler cable deliberately looped behind its hinge. The specialist connected the battery, logged the temperature, and noticed a row of names written beneath the cabinet shelf. Each name belonged to a village the courier had planned to visit.

The lights went out as the courier fastened the medicine case to the bicycle. The cooler’s small indicator remained green. Before leaving, the courier added one more village to the list, then set off while the clinic staff held lamps along the road.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors certified the clinic and kept the medicine cold until departure.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s medics retained control of the clinic and chose another route for the courier.
endings.draw: The medicine remained cold, and both parties signed the courier’s route sheet.

paragraphs: An orbital cargo gallery developed a crack across its observation window during a transfer of medical supplies. {{heroPlayer}}’s watch escorted a repairer to the seal; {{otherPlayer}}’s dock workers held the cargo lift below. Outside the glass, a medicine case drifted past with its tether cut.

{{hero}} covered the gallery door while the repairer fixed a temporary patch. A figure tried to reach the pressure controls, and the fighter held them back until the patch sealed. Through the clear section of glass, the repairer spotted the loose case hooked beneath a loading arm.

The lift brought the case inside under the dock workers’ guidance. Its cold indicator still showed a safe temperature, but a child’s drawing had been taped to the latch: a crooked flower with a note asking the medicine to arrive before tomorrow.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s watch held the gallery and recovered the supplies for delivery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers secured the gallery and took custody of the medicine case.
endings.draw: The window was patched and the medicine stayed cold while both crews prepared its delivery.

paragraphs: A mountain settlement kept an underground fire refuge that had never been tested. Smoke from a brushfire reached its upper vent before the first families arrived. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue workers took the lower entrance; {{otherPlayer}}’s local guides knew a second passage that had collapsed years before.

{{hero}} opened the vent housing and found its filter fitted backward. The specialist turned it around, cleared ash from the intake, and tested the airflow with a strip of cloth. Fresh air drew through the refuge as families came down the steps carrying blankets and a cage of restless birds.

Inside, a guide pointed to glow marks on the tunnel wall. They were an old route map, visible only after the lights went out, and led to a third exit beyond the collapsed passage. Children counted the marks while the rescue workers checked every door.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s workers secured the refuge and kept clean air flowing for the families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guides controlled the refuge and directed arrivals through their known route.
endings.draw: The families sheltered safely, and both groups traced the old map to its third exit.

paragraphs: At a riverside paper mill, an apprentice was printing invitations for a neighborhood festival when the waterwheel jammed. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came to recover a disputed print drum; {{otherPlayer}}’s mill workers wanted to finish the invitations first. Wet sheets hung like curtains across the shop floor.

{{hero}} pushed through the hanging paper and found the apprentice pinned against a turning feed arm. A stranger lunged for the release lever, and the fighter kept them back while pulling the apprentice clear. The drum stopped with one sheet halfway through its rollers, revealing a sketch beneath the festival lettering.

The sketch showed the mill decades earlier, drawn by the apprentice’s grandfather, who had carved the drum. The workers hung the unfinished sheet where everyone could see it. As the wheel was restarted, the river carried the first finished invitation downstream.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the drum after the apprentice finished the invitations.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s mill workers kept the drum and resumed their printing.
endings.draw: The invitations were completed, and both parties agreed to preserve the newly revealed sketch.

paragraphs: An elevated public garden was closing for repairs on the night of its annual lantern walk. {{heroPlayer}}’s maintenance crew came to assess a sagging pond; {{otherPlayer}}’s volunteers hoped to keep the path open. Water seeped across the paving, carrying tiny lantern reflections toward the stair.

{{hero}} followed the flow under the pond’s edge and found a blocked overflow pipe beneath a carved bench. The specialist cleared it with a narrow tool and watched the pond settle against its stone lip. Inside the pipe was a lacquered wooden token shaped like one of the garden’s missing lanterns.

The volunteers hung the token at the beginning of the walk. Visitors paused to read a name carved on its reverse, then took the dry path around the pond. Above them, the first lanterns made moving stars among the garden’s leaves.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the pond and reopened the garden path.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s volunteers retained the garden and limited the walk to its safe side.
endings.draw: The lantern walk continued on a shortened route while both groups checked the pond.

paragraphs: A street market lost power just as its cooks began an annual night meal. {{heroPlayer}}’s protection detail accompanied an electrician to the substation; {{otherPlayer}}’s vendors stood beside unlit stalls full of food. A projector inside the substation kept showing recipes on the darkened wall.

{{hero}} held the gate while the electrician traced a damaged feed. Someone came through the alley toward the open panel, and the fighter kept them clear of its exposed wiring until the breaker was reset. Light returned to the stalls, but the projector lingered on a handwritten recipe for a dish no vendor remembered.

An older cook read the recipe aloud and recognized her mother’s measurements, including an instruction to feed the first visitor who arrived late. A child stepped into the market as the pots warmed again. The cook filled a bowl before asking why the child had come.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail secured the substation and restored power to the meal.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s vendors controlled the substation and arranged their own repair crew.
endings.draw: The stalls reopened, and both groups shared food beneath the still-running projector.

paragraphs: A library had been built around a living tree, with its catalog carved into smooth panels between the roots. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came to save the tree after its leaves browned overnight; {{otherPlayer}}’s archivists feared repairs would erase the oldest titles. An unmarked panel had swollen shut.

{{hero}} lifted the panel gently and exposed a dry irrigation channel beneath it. The specialist reopened the channel while the archivists copied the hidden carving on the wood’s underside. Water ran toward the roots, carrying a loose paper label from an unseen pocket deeper inside.

At dusk, the first leaves uncurling above the reading tables cast moving shadows over the copied titles. The paper label named a book none of the archivists had seen. It was still there, lodged beyond the pocket, waiting for someone with smaller hands.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers restored the water supply and kept the tree library open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s archivists retained the library and sealed the panel until the carvings were copied.
endings.draw: The roots received water, and both teams preserved the newly uncovered catalog.

paragraphs: A neighborhood puppet theater had been closed after its revolving stage began turning by itself. {{heroPlayer}}’s restorers entered through the ticket office; {{otherPlayer}}’s performers waited in the square with their costumes. Each rotation stopped at a painted door that did not appear in the stage plan.

{{hero}} stepped below the stage and found a loose counterweight rubbing against the drive. The specialist secured it, then turned the stage by hand until the painted door aligned with a shallow alcove. Inside stood a tiny puppet with no strings, wrapped in a note about a show canceled long ago.

The performers carried the puppet into the square before the doors reopened. An elderly neighbor knew the canceled show by heart and supplied its first line. As the stage made one smooth turn, the performers repeated it and let the audience choose the next.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s restorers secured the revolving stage and reopened the theater.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s performers retained the theater and held rehearsals outside until repairs were approved.
endings.draw: The stage turned safely, and both groups stayed for the recovered show.

paragraphs: A freight car full of unassembled school desks stopped beside a shuttered village classroom. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to unload it; {{otherPlayer}}’s rail workers warned that the car’s brake could release on the slope. Through the open door, someone was shifting the heavy crates toward the edge.

{{hero}} climbed into the car and pulled a worker clear as a crate slid across the floor. Another person reached for the brake wheel, and the fighter held them back while the escort chocked the wheels. When the nearest crate broke open, a child’s carefully sharpened pencils rolled between the desk panels.

The rail workers helped carry the panels into the classroom. A teacher set one unfinished desk by the window and placed the pencils in a cup for whoever arrived first. Outside, the freight car sat still while its brake was repaired.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort secured the freight car and delivered the desks to the school.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s rail workers retained the car and delayed unloading until the brake was fixed.
endings.draw: The car was made safe, and both crews assembled the first desks together.

paragraphs: On a windy plateau, an old parade mast had been repurposed to measure gusts for a rescue flight. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort brought a weather reader to the mast; {{otherPlayer}}’s flight crew needed a reliable signal before landing. A loose canvas sail beat against the upper crossbar.

{{hero}} covered the narrow base while the reader climbed to free the tangled gauge. A figure tried to cut the mast’s ground cable, and the fighter kept them away until the gauge was secured. The loosened sail opened overhead, showing painted colors from a parade the plateau had once hosted.

The rescue aircraft approached along the course indicated by the repaired gauge. After it landed, a passenger recognized the colors and asked why the parade had stopped. The oldest crew member answered that the mast had never stopped waiting for it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort held the mast and guided the rescue flight onto the plateau.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s flight crew took charge of the mast and chose the landing window.
endings.draw: The aircraft landed safely, and both groups lowered the old sail for repair.

paragraphs: An urban bird observatory went silent on the first day of migration. {{heroPlayer}}’s volunteers climbed to its glass dome; {{otherPlayer}}’s street crew had found a loose pane above a busy crossing. Several birds perched outside wearing colored tags from another continent.

{{hero}} braced the pane and reset the observatory’s tracking lens while the street crew cleared the pavement below. The specialist read the first returning tag, then noticed its listed destination was an address in the same neighborhood. The bird had crossed an ocean only to land within sight of its intended window.

A resident at that address appeared with a shallow dish of water and said the bird had visited every year since she was young. When it settled on her sill, the observatory screen finally registered a complete route, a thin line ending exactly there.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s volunteers repaired the dome and recorded the returning birds.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s street crew secured the pane and kept the observatory closed for inspection.
endings.draw: The crossing stayed safe, and both groups watched the tagged bird complete its journey.

paragraphs: A hillside water clock measured the hours for a scattered settlement until its upper basin ran dry. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards accompanied a mason to the tower; {{otherPlayer}}’s water keepers suspected the inlet had been diverted. The clock hand was fixed at the hour when the town’s old spring had disappeared.

{{hero}} held the exposed stair while the mason checked the basin. A figure at the top reached for the stone gate, and the fighter forced them back from the mason’s ladder. Behind the gate, water pressed against a wall of roots, enough to refill the clock if the roots could be moved gently.

The mason cleared a channel around the roots, and the hand began to turn again. Residents heard the first chime from houses farther down the hillside. In the wet stone under the basin, someone had carved the spring’s original name.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards secured the tower and brought the water clock back into service.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers retained the tower and managed the inlet repair.
endings.draw: The chime sounded again as both teams agreed on a safe channel around the roots.

paragraphs: Two rescue crews reached a weather cabin at opposite ends of a whiteout, each carrying orders to use its emergency transmitter. {{heroPlayer}}’s crew had a stranded climber’s coordinates; {{otherPlayer}}’s crew had news of a bridge collapse below. Only one channel remained clear through the storm.

{{hero}} opened the transmitter casing and found a spare crystal taped beneath the battery. The specialist fitted it into the second channel while the two crew leaders held their maps together under one lamp. Both calls went out: one toward the climber, the other toward the bridge.

An answer came first from the climber, who could see the cabin’s lantern through the snow. Then a road worker reported that the bridge had been closed before anyone crossed. The crews left both maps pinned to the wall for the next storm.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew kept the cabin and coordinated the climber’s rescue.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the transmitter and managed both emergency calls.
endings.draw: Both crews shared the cabin until the climber reached shelter and the bridge was secured.

paragraphs: A polar aquarium received warm-water larvae for a breeding trial just as its heating loop froze. {{heroPlayer}}’s marine biologists arrived with portable tanks; {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew planned to drain the loop before the pipes burst. Tiny shapes swam toward the last patch of warmth.

{{hero}} disconnected the frozen return line and passed the larvae into an insulated tank without changing their temperature too quickly. The specialist then found the heater’s fault in a salt-crusted contact. As the line warmed, an older biologist recognized the larvae from a vanished reef recorded in her first field notebook.

The station crew hung the notebook page beside the tank. In the water, the larvae gathered around a small piece of reef stone carried with them across the ice. Outside the aquarium glass, snow fell over a landscape none of them would ever inhabit.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s biologists kept the larvae warm and took charge of the breeding tanks.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew retained the aquarium and replaced its damaged heating line.
endings.draw: The larvae survived, and both teams agreed on a careful temperature schedule.

paragraphs: At a snowbound post house, a mail carrier found a sack of letters frozen behind a service door. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to clear the route; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain wardens wanted the post house closed before the roof shed its ice. One envelope bore a bright stamp from the coming year.

{{hero}} held the service door while the carrier pulled the sack free. Someone tried to force the door shut from the corridor, and the fighter grappled them away from the hinge as ice broke loose above. The carrier escaped into the yard with the stamped letter dry inside a glove.

The letter had been addressed to a child expected at the post house next winter. Its writer had planned to send a welcome before leaving for the mountains. The carrier placed it in a new satchel, promising to deliver it when the child finally arrived.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort secured the post house and saved the frozen letters.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens closed the building and directed the mail recovery.
endings.draw: The mail was saved, and both groups waited for the roof to be cleared before leaving.

paragraphs: A public bath fed by a geothermal spring lost heat during the coldest week of winter. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors came to test the water; {{otherPlayer}}’s local caretakers feared a hidden leak beneath the children’s changing room. Paper boats left in the empty pool pointed toward the same drain.

{{hero}} followed the drain below the floor and found the hot-water valve jammed by a small brass key. The specialist removed it and restored the flow, then carried the key upstairs for the caretakers to identify. It fit a storage cupboard that no one had opened since the bath’s founder died.

Inside the cupboard were towels stitched with names, ready for families who had never been able to pay. The water warmed while the caretakers laid them along a bench. The children launched their paper boats again when the pool was declared safe.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors reopened the bath and recorded the source of the blockage.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers retained the bath and completed the heating repair.
endings.draw: The pool warmed, and both groups helped return the founder’s towels to use.

paragraphs: An avalanche beacon began sounding above a mountain shelter that should have been empty. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue party set out with a heat sled; {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew watched a second slide forming across the only pass. Under the beacon’s signal was a faint voice reading numbers aloud.

{{hero}} covered the exposed traverse while two rescuers reached the beacon. Movement appeared near a ridge marker, and the fighter held that position until the sled crossed. Beside the beacon, the rescuers found a surveyor counting the shelter’s remaining oxygen tanks so anyone listening would know how long they had.

The surveyor rode down under a thermal blanket, still counting until a rescuer told them the last tank could wait. In the shelter window, a lamp blinked twice: the station crew had seen the sled reach safe ground before the second slide began.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s party held the traverse and brought the surveyor into shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew controlled the pass and directed the descent from below.
endings.draw: The surveyor reached shelter, and both crews stayed clear of the slope until it settled.

paragraphs: A mountain shrine kept a heated handrail for travelers crossing its icy steps. {{heroPlayer}}’s guides brought a stranded group toward it; {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers were testing why the rail had gone cold. In the snow beside the shrine, six sets of prints arrived but only five continued.

{{hero}} reached the stair landing as a stranger shoved a caretaker toward its open hatch. The fighter pulled the caretaker back, kept the hatch clear, and sent a guide below to check the heating line. There, beneath the steps, the missing traveler sat with frozen hands wrapped around a warm pipe.

The rail grew warm again before the group climbed down. The traveler had followed the pipe after noticing its steam and had left the hatch ajar to mark the way. At the bottom step, six sets of prints turned together toward the village.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guides secured the shrine stair and brought the traveler home.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s caretakers retained the shrine and directed the evacuation.
endings.draw: The rail was repaired, and both groups walked the six travelers down together.

paragraphs: At the edge of a frozen lake, an ice lantern festival had been canceled because the lake was cracking. {{heroPlayer}}’s safety crew came to remove the lanterns; {{otherPlayer}}’s village musicians wanted to retrieve a harp left on the island. From the far shore came a single plucked note.

{{hero}} tested the old rope crossing and found its anchor buried in soft snow. The specialist shifted it onto bare rock and sent a light sled toward the island. The musicians brought the harp back without stepping onto the lake, its strings sounding whenever the wind caught them.

On shore, the musicians tuned the harp beneath one rescued lantern. Its owner, who had believed it lost, arrived to hear a tune made strange by the cold. The first ice crack sounded again in the distance as the last lantern was put out.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the rope crossing and recovered the instrument.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s musicians retained the festival site and retrieved the harp under their direction.
endings.draw: The lake was closed, and both parties listened to one final song on shore.

paragraphs: A wool dye house above the snowline was running its last winter batch when its drive belt snapped. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came for blankets promised to an isolated clinic; {{otherPlayer}}’s dyers feared the exposed wheel would tear their cloth. Red yarn trailed across the floor toward a jammed spindle.

{{hero}} pulled a dyer away as someone shoved the spindle toward the turning wheel. The fighter held the intruder back and braced the wheel while workers cut the belt. Freed from the machine, the cloth opened into a half-finished blanket stitched with a patient’s name.

The dyers finished the edge by hand beside a stove. By nightfall, the named blanket and the others were folded onto a sled, still warm from the room. A child at the clinic door recognized the stitching before the escort read the tag.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the blankets and carried them to the clinic.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s dyers held the dye house and arranged their own delivery.
endings.draw: The wheel stopped safely, and both crews helped finish the blankets by hand.

paragraphs: A roadside bakery kept its oven burning through a blizzard so passing convoys could find the village. {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts came to mark its location; {{otherPlayer}}’s bakers worried that the wood store had been emptied. The oven still glowed, and floury footprints led into the storm.

{{hero}} covered the outer door while a scout followed the footprints to the buried woodshed. A figure appeared between the shed and the oven, but the fighter held the line until the scout came back with a sled of fuel. In the shed was a stack of bread wrapped for travelers who had never arrived.

The bakers loaded the bread beside the fire and waited for a horn from the road. It sounded faintly before dawn. When the first convoy stopped, each traveler was handed a loaf still warm enough to steam in the snow.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s scouts secured the bakery as a guide point for the convoy.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s bakers kept control of the oven and directed arrivals from the road.
endings.draw: The oven stayed lit, and both parties helped feed the travelers who followed its glow.

paragraphs: A survey shuttle needed an emergency runway across a snowfield where old runway lamps lay buried. {{heroPlayer}}’s ground crew came to uncover them; {{otherPlayer}}’s avalanche watchers warned that digging along the slope would disturb the crust. In the sky, the shuttle’s descent light blinked faster.

{{hero}} traced the lamp cable beneath the snow without cutting into the crust and connected a portable power cell at the lowest marker. A row of small lights emerged through the drift one by one, pointing away from the dangerous slope. The pilot altered course toward the new line.

The shuttle slid to a halt in a cloud of powder. Inside, a surveyor held a bundle of field notes against a fogged window and smiled when the lamps came into view. The avalanche watchers kept their eyes on the upper slope until the passengers reached shelter.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew lit the runway and brought the shuttle down safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watchers controlled the snowfield and selected another landing approach.
endings.draw: The shuttle landed beyond the unstable crust, and both crews marked the lamps for future flights.

paragraphs: A weather balloon had snagged on the mast of an isolated school, pulling at the only radio aerial for miles. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol came to recover the balloon; {{otherPlayer}}’s teachers kept their pupils indoors as ice fell from the mast. A message could be seen inside the balloon’s clear instrument pouch.

{{hero}} covered the schoolyard while a technician climbed to free the snag. A figure moved behind the mast and reached for the aerial cable, but the fighter kept them from the technician’s ladder. The balloon floated down with its pouch intact, its message written on the back of a weather chart.

The chart came from another school on the far side of the pass, where children had drawn a sun and asked whether anyone had seen it that week. The local pupils drew their own answer beside the radio and waited for the aerial to carry it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol secured the school mast and returned the balloon safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s teachers kept the schoolyard closed and directed the aerial repair.
endings.draw: The aerial stayed intact, and both groups helped send the children’s reply.

paragraphs: A herd of elk gathered at a frozen river crossing just as a snowplow reached its narrow bridge. {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers wanted a safe path for the animals; {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew needed the bridge open for medicine deliveries. The elk would not approach the ice beneath the bridge.

{{hero}} followed the bank and found a shallow gravel ford hidden by snow. The specialist tested its footing, placed bright markers, and led the first elk across without bringing it onto the bridge. The road crew held the plow still while the rest of the herd followed.

The plow crossed after the last animal had climbed the far bank. In its wake came a small delivery sled, its driver carrying medicine to the next town. The rangers watched one young elk turn back toward the marked ford, then vanish after the herd.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rangers secured the ford and reopened the bridge for deliveries.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew retained the bridge and controlled the timing of the crossing.
endings.draw: The herd and medicine both crossed safely, and the markers stayed until the thaw.

paragraphs: A cliffside infirmary used a narrow sunroom to help patients recover through the long dark season. {{heroPlayer}}’s medical team came to restore its failed shutters; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain workers warned that daylight reflecting off the snow could overheat the glass. A patient had painted a blue horizon across the lowest pane.

{{hero}} reset the shutter stops to admit a thin band of afternoon light, then measured the room’s temperature beside the patient’s chair. The specialist adjusted the last slat until the light fell exactly along the painted horizon. The patient held a hand in it and asked for a brush.

By evening, a second horizon ran above the first, this one gold. The workers left the shutters at their careful angle, and patients took turns sitting in the band of warmth. Outside, the real horizon had already disappeared behind the cliff.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s medical team reopened the sunroom at a safe temperature.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the shutters and kept the room closed for inspection.
endings.draw: The sunroom warmed gently, and both teams agreed to check the glass each afternoon.

paragraphs: A bell rang beneath the ice of a disused memorial garden, though the bell tower had been empty for years. {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers followed the sound across the path; {{otherPlayer}}’s gardeners feared the thawing soil would swallow the old markers. The bell rang again when everyone stood still.

{{hero}} reached a frozen maintenance grate as someone tried to shove a searcher into its open shaft. The fighter caught the searcher, drove the person back, and held the grate steady while a rope was lowered. Below, a caretaker pulled twice on a bell cord and called out through the dark.

The caretaker emerged carrying an armful of fallen nameplates, collected before meltwater could wash them away. Gardeners set the plates along the path in order. When the last was replaced, the caretaker rang the bell once from aboveground.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers rescued the caretaker and secured the grate.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s gardeners retained the memorial garden and directed the recovery.
endings.draw: The caretaker returned safely, and both groups reset the rescued nameplates.

paragraphs: An icebound cargo ship began sounding its foghorn on a day without fog. {{heroPlayer}}’s boarding team came to inspect the bridge; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor crew had seen a cable trailing from its stern toward the shore. Children at the quay recognized the horn’s unusual three-note pattern.

{{hero}} covered the wheelhouse door while a mechanic traced the cable. A figure tried to pull the ship’s power lead loose, but the fighter held the passage until the mechanic found a battery connected to the horn. It had been wired to a small clock set to sound every hour.

An older harbor worker listened to the next three notes and remembered them from ships that had carried families out of the port during a winter evacuation. The children copied the pattern on a piece of paper while the crew made the clock safe.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the wheelhouse and brought the ship’s horn under control.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor crew retained the ship and disconnected the cable from shore.
endings.draw: The harbor stayed safe while both parties recorded the old horn pattern.

paragraphs: A heated transit tent at the mountain pass filled with travelers after snow closed the road. {{heroPlayer}}’s medics arrived to check their supplies; {{otherPlayer}}’s pass wardens counted beds for the night. One cot remained made up with a blanket folded over a pillow, though nobody claimed it.

{{hero}} discovered that the tent’s second heater had been disconnected and its fuel diverted to a buried kettle. The specialist restored the heater, then lifted the kettle to find broth still warm inside. A traveler said the missing cot belonged to the cook, who had gone out to meet a late bus.

The bus arrived with its lights dim under snow, and the cook stepped in carrying three more passengers’ bags. They shared the broth before lying down. In the morning, the cot was empty again: its blanket had been moved to the bus for the next stranded traveler.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s medics kept the tent warm and treated its new arrivals.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens controlled the tent and assigned the remaining beds.
endings.draw: Every traveler found warmth, and both teams helped prepare the tent for the next bus.

paragraphs: An ice sculpture hall kept its doors open through a rolling blackout so children could see the annual lantern exhibition. {{heroPlayer}}’s gallery crew came to guard the emergency generator; {{otherPlayer}}’s maintenance staff found its fuel line exposed. A lantern inside the tallest sculpture still burned.

{{hero}} reached the generator as a stranger tried to slam its service hatch on a technician’s arm. The fighter forced the hatch open and pulled the technician clear while the fuel line was capped. By the lantern’s light, a child found the way out through the exhibition’s twisting corridors.

When power returned, the child asked the artist why the tallest sculpture showed an empty chair. The artist answered that it was meant for the person who had never made it to the first exhibition. The lantern was left burning beside the chair until closing.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the generator and reopened the hall to visitors.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff took charge of the hall and completed the generator repair.
endings.draw: The children left safely, and both groups checked the lanterns before the exhibition resumed.

paragraphs: A cinema cut into a snowbank was screening a silent film when its projector began throwing a second image onto the ceiling. {{heroPlayer}}’s projectionists went to the booth; {{otherPlayer}}’s safety crew feared heat from the lamp was melting the roof. In the upper image, a person seemed to wave from an empty street.

{{hero}} lowered the lamp power and found a second reel threaded behind the first. The specialist separated them without tearing either strip, letting the ceiling image settle onto the screen. It showed footage of the street outside the cinema on its opening night, with a crowd waving into the camera.

The audience recognized a younger version of the ticket seller near the front of that crowd. She stood beneath the screen with her stub in hand and counted faces until she found the friend who had once dragged her inside. Outside, snow kept falling over the same street.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s projectionists secured the booth and finished the recovered screening.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s safety crew closed the cinema until the lamp and roof were checked.
endings.draw: The reels were preserved, and both parties stayed to watch the opening-night footage.

paragraphs: A cable lift stopped halfway up a glacier with a single passenger waving from its window. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue crew reached the lower station; {{otherPlayer}}’s lift operators had found a frayed guide line. Through the cabin glass, the passenger held up a small white flag.

{{hero}} reached the maintenance platform as a stranger tried to force the brake release with a crowbar. The fighter pulled them away from the lever and held it steady while an operator lowered the cabin by hand. Inside, the passenger used the flag to wrap a cracked window so blowing snow could not enter.

Back at the station, the passenger unfolded the flag. It carried a child’s drawing of the glacier as it looked before the lift was built. The operator hung it beside the route map while the cabin’s guide line was replaced.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the lift and brought its passenger down safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s operators retained the station and ran the manual descent.
endings.draw: The passenger returned, and both teams kept the lift closed until its line was replaced.

paragraphs: A shelter directory began directing walkers to cabins buried by an overnight drift. {{heroPlayer}}’s data team came to correct it; {{otherPlayer}}’s trail wardens had already placed hand-painted signs at the junction. The directory’s screen showed a shelter moving slowly across the map.

{{hero}} traced the shelter’s beacon to a sled parked beneath snow beside the junction. The specialist switched its tag from a fixed building to a mobile rescue station and updated the public map. The trail wardens uncovered the sled and found its heaters working, with a thermos waiting inside.

A walker arrived as the new map appeared, confused to find a shelter that had come to meet them. The wardens gave the walker tea before explaining the change. On the screen, the shelter’s little icon stayed beside the junction while the drift grew deeper.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team repaired the directory and deployed the sled as a safe shelter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens retained the junction and guided walkers using their signs.
endings.draw: The route was corrected, and both groups kept the heated sled at the junction.

paragraphs: A glacial prism inside a cliffside observatory began splitting moonlight into colors that appeared on the valley floor. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers came to examine it; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol worried that people were crossing the ice to follow the lights. At the far end, a cluster of lanterns was moving toward open water.

{{hero}} covered the observatory threshold while a researcher shifted the prism away from the lake. Someone reached for the mount, and the fighter held the entrance until it was locked. The colored path withdrew from the ice; across the valley, the lanterns stopped and turned toward shore.

When the lantern carriers arrived, they showed the researchers a photograph taken from below. The prism had cast a pattern like a road complete with bright crossings. An old map on the observatory wall showed a road there once, long before the lake spread over it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers secured the prism and guided the lantern carriers to shore.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol controlled the observatory and closed the lake approach.
endings.draw: The lantern carriers returned safely, and both groups kept the prism turned from the ice.

paragraphs: An avalanche had buried the haul line of a hillside stone quarry. {{heroPlayer}}’s laborers arrived to retrieve a trapped tool cart; {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew wanted the quarry sealed until the slope settled. A red ribbon tied to the cart showed through the snow like a warning.

{{hero}} reached the haul lever as another person pulled at it from the far side, risking the cart’s plunge. The fighter grappled them away from the handle and held the brake while the laborers dug the cart free. Beneath its tarp lay a carved stone bench intended for the village school.

The road crew cleared a path below the slope, and the bench was carried out without using the line. Children brushed snow from its seat when it reached the schoolyard. Someone had carved a small ruler along the edge for measuring how much they grew each year.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s laborers secured the cart and delivered the bench to the school.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s road crew retained the quarry and postponed the recovery.
endings.draw: The bench reached the school while both groups kept the unstable haul line closed.

paragraphs: A lighthouse above a frozen harbor began flashing toward the inland hills instead of the sea. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal crew came to find the fault; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor workers needed the beam back before a supply convoy crossed the ice. The lamps had been aimed by hand, not by the automatic drive.

{{hero}} opened the drive casing and found a second switch labeled with the name of a former keeper. The specialist tested it and watched the beam strike a narrow road beyond the hills. There, a stranded truck answered with its headlights, then began following the light toward the harbor.

The harbor workers took over the seaward warning while the truck came down the hill. Its driver said the keeper had once promised a light for anyone lost on that road. When the truck reached shore, the beam was turned back to the ice route.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew controlled the lighthouse and guided both the truck and convoy safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the light and prioritized the ice crossing.
endings.draw: Both routes received a warning beam in turn, and the truck and convoy reached shelter.

paragraphs: A meteor survey crew discovered an exposed sheet of black glass at the center of a snowy crater. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts wanted to scan it before the next storm; {{otherPlayer}}’s rangers kept curious visitors behind a ridge. In reflected sunlight, the glass showed a grove where the crater now lay.

{{hero}} stabilized the scanning frame on uneven snow and captured the reflected grove before cloud shadow covered the glass. The specialist noticed one tree bearing a white ribbon in every frame. A ranger brought an old landscape photograph from the station; the ribbon marked the family picnic tree.

The clouds opened once more and the grove returned for a breath, superimposed on the crater’s bare stone. The family who owned the photograph stood silently beside the ridge. Then the sunlight shifted and the glass reflected only their faces.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts secured the crater and preserved the image for the family.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s rangers closed the crater and retained its survey records.
endings.draw: The image was recorded, and both groups agreed to protect the glass from the storm.

paragraphs: A ski gondola stopped above an empty slope with a passenger pressing both palms against the window. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescue team reached the upper station; {{otherPlayer}}’s mechanics were lowering a service cradle from below. Snow hid the point where the main cable had slipped from its guide.

{{hero}} reached the guide housing as a stranger tried to force its lock while the cable was loaded. The fighter dragged them clear, kept the housing closed, and gave the mechanics time to ease the gondola onto the service cradle. The passenger stepped out carrying a violin case held tight beneath a coat.

At the station, the passenger opened the case and found the instrument unharmed. They played a few notes while the mechanics checked the cable, more to steady their hands than to entertain anyone. The snow carried the sound down to the empty slope.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers secured the cable and brought the passenger to the upper station.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s mechanics retained the lift and completed the recovery from below.
endings.draw: The passenger returned safely, and both teams kept the gondola idle for repair.

paragraphs: An alpine star station stopped publishing its nightly sky map after one constellation vanished from its display. {{heroPlayer}}’s instrument team climbed to the dome; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain guides kept visitors below the wind line. A handwritten chart beside the telescope showed the missing stars exactly where they belonged.

{{hero}} checked the tracking gears and found the dome’s calibration ring had slipped by a fraction of a degree. The specialist aligned it using the handwritten chart, then watched the missing constellation return to the display. Beneath it appeared a tiny sequence of dots the instrument had rejected as noise.

An older guide recognized the dots as a signal lamp on a distant ridge, visible on clear nights when she was young. The team turned the telescope that way. Through the glass, one lamp answered from a cabin everyone had believed empty for years.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the dome and restored its sky map.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guides retained the station and limited access during the wind.
endings.draw: The map was restored, and both groups kept the telescope on the distant lamp.

paragraphs: A snowbound relay station began repeating a distress call from a valley whose settlement had been evacuated years earlier. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal crew came to trace it; {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol had heard faint knocking inside the locked transmitter room. The call included a voice counting backward from ten.

{{hero}} covered the entrance while a technician opened the transmitter casing. Someone approached across the roof with a cutting tool, and the fighter kept them away from the aerial. Inside the casing was a hand-wound recorder, still playing the same short call each time a loose contact touched.

The technician stopped the recorder before it reached one. In the silence, the knocking came again from a storage closet behind the transmitter. A former station worker stepped out carrying the key to the evacuated settlement’s final supply cache.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew held the relay and recovered the location of the supply cache.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the station and took charge of the old call.
endings.draw: The transmission was preserved, and both groups followed the worker’s directions.

paragraphs: At a mountain race station, a line of sleds waited for a course marker that had toppled in the night. {{heroPlayer}}’s marshals came to reset it; {{otherPlayer}}’s rescue volunteers wanted the course closed until the ice was checked. One racer was already overdue from a practice run.

{{hero}} reached the marker as a stranger tried to drag its base onto unsafe ice. The fighter seized the pole, pulled the stranger back to firm ground, and planted the bright flag where the volunteers had tested the surface. Far off, a sled appeared, steering toward the new mark.

The overdue racer arrived exhausted, carrying a lost competitor’s scarf. They had gone off course together; the other racer waited in a sheltered hollow, too tired to move. The volunteers took a rescue sled past the flag while the marshals held the course clear.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s marshals secured the station and guided both racers to safety.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s volunteers closed the course and directed the rescue.
endings.draw: The race was postponed, and both teams followed the flag to the stranded racer.

paragraphs: A border aid depot was giving out blankets when its numbering machine printed the same address on every parcel. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors arrived to audit the deliveries; {{otherPlayer}}’s volunteers feared families would receive nothing before the pass closed. One parcel already had a child’s handprint in blue ink.

{{hero}} traced the fault to a bent plate in the machine and replaced it with the correct route grid. The specialist sorted the parcels by destination, keeping the handprinted one aside until its label could be checked. On its underside was a note asking for two blankets, one for a neighbor.

The parcels left on separate sleds while the volunteers held the depot doors against the snow. The child who had marked the parcel returned for a receipt. When shown the new address, the child pointed to the neighbor’s house across the lane and smiled.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors repaired the route grid and sent the parcels to their proper homes.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s volunteers retained the depot and hand-sorted the remaining deliveries.
endings.draw: Every parcel received an address, and both parties sent the sleds out before the pass closed.

paragraphs: An orbital ice harvester brought back a clear block containing a moving point of light. {{heroPlayer}}’s watch escorted a technician to the unloading bay; {{otherPlayer}}’s cold-room staff wanted the block sealed before it warmed. A thin crack ran from the light toward the floor.

{{hero}} covered the bay entrance as a figure tried to cut power to the cooling frame. The fighter held the passage while the technician stabilized the block and moved it under glass. The moving point settled against the crack, revealing itself as a tiny reflection from a warning beacon beyond the window.

The staff followed the reflected line to an emergency pod drifting beside the harvester. Someone inside tapped the glass in the same rhythm as the warning beacon. The ice was left in the cold room while the watch went to bring the pod aboard.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s watch held the bay and launched the pod recovery.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff retained the cold room and directed the unloading.
endings.draw: The pod was found, and both teams kept the ice block stable under glass.

paragraphs: Deep beneath a glacier, an air-driven warning organ fell silent while meltwater rose toward a drilling camp. {{heroPlayer}}’s tunnel crew went to restart it; {{otherPlayer}}’s drillers were still working beyond the last bend. A low note sounded once, then stopped with a hiss.

{{hero}} reached the organ’s valves and found ice holding one whistle open, stealing air from the others. The specialist cleared it and played the camp’s warning sequence through the pipes. Up ahead, drill motors fell quiet one by one; the crew there had heard the signal.

The drillers came back around the bend carrying their logs dry beneath their coats. A wall of meltwater slid across the work face moments later. When everyone reached the upper tunnel, the smallest pipe still hummed a single note on the remaining air.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the warning organ and evacuated the drillers.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s drillers retained the tunnel and directed its closure.
endings.draw: The camp emptied before the flood, and both teams kept the organ ready at the upper passage.

paragraphs: A winter bathhouse had closed its hot spring after steam began escaping through a painted folding screen. {{heroPlayer}}’s restorers came for the screen; {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants wanted to keep the building warm for stranded travelers. Behind the painted mountains, a pipe hammered against the wall.

{{hero}} entered the narrow service room as a stranger tried to force the steam valve open. The fighter seized their arm and pulled them from the scalding pipe while an attendant closed the feed. The screen folded away to reveal an older painting of summer fields on its reverse.

The attendants moved the screen into a dry room where travelers could see both seasons. A restorer touched the summer painting and found a date beneath the frame: it had been made in the same winter as the bathhouse’s first recorded snowfall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s restorers secured the screen and helped make the bathhouse safe.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s attendants retained the building and managed the steam repair.
endings.draw: The travelers stayed warm in a safe room while both parties preserved the painted screen.

paragraphs: A snow-covered schoolyard marked the spot where former pupils had buried a time capsule. {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers came to recover it before a foundation survey; {{otherPlayer}}’s builders had already laid out the new classroom. On an old sketch, the burial mark stood beneath a tree that was gone.

{{hero}} matched the sketch’s long winter shadows to the remaining wall and located a small iron lid beneath the snow. The specialist lifted it without breaking the foundation markers. Inside the capsule was a stack of predictions, each signed by a child imagining what the school might become.

The builders read one prediction aloud: a room with windows wide enough to see the whole mountain. They turned their new plan toward the ridge, where afternoon sun was just reaching the yard. The capsule went indoors for the pupils to open together.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caretakers recovered the capsule and protected the schoolyard site.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s builders retained the site and scheduled the capsule opening before construction.
endings.draw: The capsule was saved, and both groups brought its predictions into the new classroom plan.

paragraphs: An aurora antenna on a high ridge began broadcasting a lullaby into nearby emergency radios. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal guards came to inspect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s mountain technicians feared the broadcast would hide weather calls. The lullaby stopped whenever clouds covered the northern lights.

{{hero}} covered the antenna platform while a technician adjusted its exposed receiver. A figure at the far cable anchor raised a weapon, and the fighter held that approach until the receiver was isolated. With the radio quiet, the technician heard the lullaby coming faintly from a music box inside the mast.

The box was wound by a tiny turbine whenever the antenna turned into the aurora wind. Someone had placed it there for a child who waited at the ridge for a parent’s return. The guards carried it down so the child could decide where it belonged.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards secured the antenna and cleared the emergency channel.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians retained the ridge and isolated the broadcast.
endings.draw: The radios worked again, and both teams delivered the music box safely.

paragraphs: A winter botanical station displayed a single living vine in a glass passage linking two dormitories. {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists came when its leaves curled overnight; {{otherPlayer}}’s station crew found frost inside the passage seal. A visitor had tied a red thread to the vine’s lowest leaf.

{{hero}} tested the passage vents and discovered warm air escaping through a latch that looked closed. The specialist reset the seal and guided a narrow stream of humid air across the plant. Its lowest leaf slowly opened, lifting the red thread clear of the frozen glass.

A visitor returned at dusk and recognized the thread from a winter when the vine had first taken root. It marked the length of that first fragile stem. The botanists left it in place as the passage warmed and footsteps resumed between the dormitories.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists restored the vine’s growing conditions and kept the passage open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the station and closed the passage for seal repairs.
endings.draw: The vine recovered, and both groups kept watch over the repaired passage.

paragraphs: A winter fair built a mirror maze beside a frozen pond, then lost its lantern keeper inside when snow covered the exits. {{heroPlayer}}’s fair guards entered by the service gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s ice inspectors wanted the pond path closed. Reflections showed the keeper’s lantern in three directions at once.

{{hero}} rounded a corner as a stranger tried to shove a guard through a mirror panel onto thin ice. The fighter caught the guard, pulled the stranger away, and found the real lantern by watching its flame flicker in the wind. The keeper was behind the next panel, shielding another lost visitor.

The guards led both visitors out along the dry service path. Once the maze was empty, the keeper turned the lantern around and showed the painted exit arrow on its base. He had been trying to hold it high enough for a reflection to carry it through the maze.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards secured the maze and brought both visitors to the fair.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors closed the pond path and directed the rescue.
endings.draw: The visitors came out safely, and both parties marked a clear route through the mirrors.

paragraphs: A mountainside mineral store held a stone that rang when the thaw reached its door. {{heroPlayer}}’s security detail accompanied a curator to inspect it; {{otherPlayer}}’s geologists feared the ringing meant the roof supports had shifted. From outside, each note sounded like a different bell.

{{hero}} covered the narrow gallery while the curator moved the stone away from a cracked support. An intruder stepped between the shelves with a tool raised, and the fighter held them back until the curator reached the exit. The stone fell silent when set on a wooden bench, though the roof kept ticking softly.

The geologists closed the store and listened from the safe side of the door. The ticking followed drops of meltwater rather than moving rock. When a curator tapped the rescued stone lightly, it rang once, clear enough for everyone to hear through the snow.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail secured the stone and escorted the curator out.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s geologists retained the store and sealed it for structural work.
endings.draw: The stone was saved, and both teams kept the building closed until its roof was checked.

paragraphs: At a geothermal field, a ring of warm ground kept a tiny winter orchard alive. {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors came to mend its broken pressure gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s field crew worried the repair would redirect heat beneath the nearby homes. Steam hid the gate and made every footstep sound close.

{{hero}} found a welder kneeling at the gate as someone rushed them through the steam. The fighter intercepted the person and held the narrow platform while the welder closed the pressure line. One of the orchard’s trees shook in the gust and dropped a single fruit into the welder’s open kit.

With the pressure stable, the field crew checked both the houses and the orchard. The welder washed the fruit in a bucket of cold water and offered it to the first resident who came out. The resident broke it in half for a child waiting beside the trees.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s contractors secured the gate and preserved the orchard’s heat.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the field and controlled the pressure repair.
endings.draw: The homes stayed warm, and both groups inspected the orchard before leaving.

paragraphs: An abandoned rail station hosted a winter art installation that projected a different shadow for each visitor. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to repair a failing projector; {{otherPlayer}}’s station stewards kept children away from its hot casing. One shadow appeared even when the hall was empty.

{{hero}} cooled the projector and aligned its warped mirror without erasing the stored images. The specialist found the extra shadow in a glass slide placed backward in the lens. Turned around, it became the silhouette of a station porter carrying two suitcases, taken on the building’s final day of service.

An older steward recognized the porter as her grandfather. She stood beneath the image and lifted an arm; for a moment their shadows touched on the wall. Children waited their turn while the technicians lowered the lamp to a safe brightness.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians restored the exhibit and kept the station hall open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s stewards retained the hall and suspended projections for repair.
endings.draw: The projector ran safely, and both parties preserved the porter’s glass slide.

paragraphs: A rope bridge above a winter gorge led to a cartographer’s unmanned survey hut. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort came to collect its map; {{otherPlayer}}’s ridge guides warned that the far anchorage had begun to slip. Across the gorge, a bright flag rose briefly from the hut and fell.

{{hero}} covered the bridge while a guide crossed to secure the anchorage. A figure at the far side reached for the guide’s rope, and the fighter held them away until the guide fixed a new line. Inside the hut, the map had been weighted down by a tin of signal flags.

The cartographer emerged from a sheltered hollow below the hut, having raised the flag when the bridge moved. She carried a fresh map showing a footpath around the gorge. The escort followed its first landmarks as the bridge swayed behind them.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort secured the hut and brought the cartographer’s new map to the ridge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guides retained the bridge and closed it until the anchorage was replaced.
endings.draw: The map was recovered, and both groups used the safer footpath around the gorge.

paragraphs: Two coastal survey crews reached the same mangrove nursery before a king tide, each convinced their instruments marked the safest channel. {{heroPlayer}}’s crew followed red floats; {{otherPlayer}}’s crew had planted blue ones. A young heron stood between the lines on a patch of exposed root.

{{hero}} waded to the root and found a current sensor tangled beneath it, its cable pulling the red floats off course. The specialist freed the sensor and rechecked both channels while the bird watched from above. The corrected readings showed a narrow passage neither set of floats had marked.

The crews moved the floats together before the water rose. The heron stepped into the branches as the tide covered its resting place. From the bank, the new passage looked like a deliberate gap left for boats and birds alike.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the nursery channel and guided the survey boats through.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the markers and chose the safe passage.
endings.draw: Both crews marked the shared channel before the king tide entered the mangroves.

paragraphs: An island tide station had sent contradictory readings to every ferry on the coast. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspection crew arrived to check its gauge; {{otherPlayer}}’s ferry pilots waited offshore for a safe depth. A caretaker stood beside the gauge, holding its missing brass pointer.

{{hero}} covered the station ramp while a mechanic reached the caretaker and returned the pointer to its axle. A figure appeared behind the empty gauge housing and tried to break the link to the shore display, but the fighter held the ramp until the mechanic restored the reading. The water was falling fast.

The pilots altered course to the deeper channel and waved as they passed the station. The caretaker explained that the pointer had come loose during a night storm and had been turning in their hand ever since, following a tide no one else could see.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the station and restored the tide reading for the ferries.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s pilots retained the channel and directed the gauge repair.
endings.draw: The ferries crossed safely, and both crews checked the restored gauge against the waterline.

paragraphs: A coastal warning station displayed an all-clear signal while families were still evacuating the low streets. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors came to find the error; {{otherPlayer}}’s flood workers were lifting doors off hinges to make stretchers. A row of names on the shelter board had been rubbed away by rain.

{{hero}} found the station’s water sensor mounted above the level of the homes it was supposed to protect. The specialist lowered it, corrected the public signal, and copied the faded shelter names from an older paper list. A volunteer read each name aloud while a worker marked the corresponding house.

By evening, every marked house had been checked. The last resident came out carrying a small chalkboard with a fresh shelter list, dry beneath a coat. The warning signal remained lit until the water began to recede from the first doorstep.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the station and kept its warning accurate through the flood.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s workers retained the streets and managed evacuation using their own markers.
endings.draw: The households were accounted for, and both groups kept the warning lit until the water fell.

paragraphs: A desalination plant stopped filling its public water tanks during a cyclone. {{heroPlayer}}’s security team brought a repairer to the intake; {{otherPlayer}}’s coastal crew kept residents away from the flooded access road. One tank still dripped, its tap left open beneath a row of empty bottles.

{{hero}} covered the intake walkway while the repairer cleared debris from a jammed pump. A figure moved toward the power switch, and the fighter held the narrow approach until the pump started. Water ran into the tank, filling the first bottle before anyone thought to close the tap.

A resident brought more bottles from the shelter and lined them along the dry side of the plant. The coastal crew counted them against the households waiting inland. Between gusts, the renewed pump made a steady sound that people at the shelter could hear.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the plant and restored water to the public tanks.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s crew retained the intake and directed the repair from the coastal side.
endings.draw: The pump held through the storm, and both teams helped fill bottles for the shelter.

paragraphs: A harbor pilot station kept a row of lanterns lit so small boats could enter during a tropical squall. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts brought replacement oil; {{otherPlayer}}’s pilots were guiding the last fishing boat around a hidden shoal. The middle lantern went dark while the boat was still outside.

{{hero}} reached the narrow lantern room as a stranger tried to drag the pilot away from its wheel. The fighter pulled the pilot free and held the doorway while a crew member refilled the lamp. Outside, the boat adjusted course toward the three lights shining together again.

The fishermen came ashore carrying a wet bundle of hand-painted harbor charts. Their grandparent had drawn the shoal before the station was built, and they had kept the charts aboard for luck. The pilots pinned one beside their modern route display.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the station and helped the fishing boat enter safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s pilots retained the lantern room and guided the boat by their own signals.
endings.draw: The boat reached shore, and both groups kept the lanterns burning through the squall.
